confirmed.statement: (a) The paper states random assignment in its own text: 'Participants were randomly assigned to one of two conditions.' Fig. 4 on the same page draws 'Random assignment to condition' with one arrow to Human-Only and one to Human+GLM. The form's assignment.quote is verbatim, and its locator is right.
confirmed.locator: PDF p. 9 (journal p. 1031), Sect. 3.2, first sentence; Fig. 4, PDF p. 9

confirmed.statement: Unit and structure: the sentence names participants as the units assigned, and no passage describes assignment by seminar, course, or session. The only other 'random' strings in the body text say that GLM ideas were shown without randomization and that shortlisted ideas were randomized for rating. The design is 'a single-factor between–subjects experiment with two conditions: human-only vs. human + GLM', so unit = individual and structure = between hold, and check (e) on the order of conditions does not apply. The paper does not describe the randomization mechanism or the allocation ratio.
confirmed.locator: PDF p. 9 (journal p. 1031), Sects. 3.2 and 3.3; PDF p. 8 (journal p. 1030), Sect. 3.1; abstract, PDF p. 1; seminars, PDF p. 10 (journal p. 1032), Sect. 3.4; rating order, PDF p. 11 (journal p. 1033), Sect. 3.6

confirmed.statement: (b) What was assigned is access to GLM ideas during the participant's own 10-minute brainstorming session, not a change in whose output is rated: 'In the human + GLM treatment, participants can request and copy GLM suggestions during their brainstorming session whenever they desire; instructions required at least one such request.' 'Only for participants in the human + GLM condition, the GLM functionality on the right was shown.' Fig. 4 marks the brainstorming step 'Unassisted' versus 'Assisted by GLM'. Both arms then shortlisted four ideas from their own long list. This matches assignment.what_was_assigned and both arms descriptions.
confirmed.locator: PDF p. 9 (journal p. 1031), Sects. 3.2 and 3.3; Fig. 4, PDF p. 9; Fig. 5, PDF p. 10

confirmed.statement: (c) The tool is a large language model: 'As a GLM, we used GPT-3.5-turbo-0301 with a temperature of 0.9'. A backend filled a pre-defined prompt template (Fig. 6) with the question, the number of ideas, the participant's idea list, and the GLM's earlier ideas for that participant, and showed three ideas per click, limited to 20 words, without filtering. Participants did not write prompts. ai_tool.name_model, role = ideas_supplied (codebook Sect. 6), and how_used match the text.
confirmed.locator: PDF p. 9 (journal p. 1031), Sect. 3.3; PDF p. 10 (journal p. 1032), Sect. 3.3 and Figs. 5-6; codebook Sect. 6, AI role

confirmed.statement: (d) The comparison arm has no AI: 'In the human-only baseline, each person brainstormed individually with the app’s GLM function deactivated.' The introduction says that in the control condition 'participants received no GLM support.' This matches arms[human-only].ai = none and the ai_vs_bau contrasts of S1-O1 to S1-O8. The paper says it chose this baseline over human groups or other support systems.
confirmed.locator: PDF p. 9, Sect. 3.2; PDF p. 3 (journal p. 1025), Sect. 1

confirmed.statement: Counts: the paper gives no count at assignment. '77 participants brainstormed and completed the survey'; two were excluded (one who misunderstood the task, condition not stated, and one human + GLM participant who made no GLM request), which leaves 75. Per-arm counts appear only as unlabeled 'group sizes of 38 and 37' in the sensitivity analysis. So participants.n_randomized = null and arms[].n_randomized and n_analyzed = null follow form rule 1. Two passages fit 37 treated (6 participants = 16.2 percent; Fig. 10 bars 3 + 5 + 14 + 11 + 4 = 37), as the form's open question says.

summary: The PDF supports every part of the assignment, arms, and ai_tool coding: participants 'were randomly assigned to one of two conditions' (PDF p. 9, Sect. 3.2, and Fig. 4) in a single-factor between-subjects design (PDF p. 8, Sect. 3.1), and the two conditions differ in whether the participant's own brainstorming app offered on-demand GPT-3.5-turbo-0301 ideas, with at least one request required, or had its GLM function deactivated. The gaps leave criterion 1 intact: the paper names no randomization mechanism, gives no count at assignment, prints only unlabeled group sizes of 38 and 37, and drops one treated participant who made no GLM request, while ai_tool.how_used omits a timeout fallback to ideas generated with the initial prompt.
